findings.evidence: Determinacy.lean:106-108 defines `H := fun _ x xi _ => if 1 < |xi| then 0 else (Icc 0 1).indicator …`; `grep '^theorem\|^lemma\|^def' GPD/Polynomiality.lean` shows `momentPolynomial` (:179), `mellinMomentGpd_polynomial` (:273), `mellinMomentH_polynomial` (:291).
findings.fix: Rename to something naming the x-profile and its support, e.g. `Model.ofQuarkPolynomialProfile`, and rename the companions (`ofPolynomial_E`, `assumptions_ofPolynomial`, `ofPolynomial_H_of_mem_Icc`, `integrable_ofPolynomial_H`, `mellinMomentH_ofPolynomial`) to match.
findings.issue: `Model.ofPolynomial` is ambiguous in this namespace: `GPD/Polynomiality.lean` already uses "polynomial" for the polynomial in ξ formed by the moments (`momentPolynomial`, `mellinMomentH_polynomial`, `mellinMomentGpd_polynomial`), so `Model.ofPolynomial p` reads as "model from a moment polynomial" rather than "model whose x-profile is p". The name also hides that H is `p` only on the quark half `[0,1]` (zero on `[-1,0)`) and only at `|ξ| ≤ 1`, unlike the canonical `Model.ofDoubleDistribution`.

findings.evidence: Determinacy.lean:130-133: `(hx : x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (hxi : |xi| ≤ 1)`; both are used in the `simp [Model.ofPolynomial, not_lt.mpr hxi, Set.indicator_of_mem hx]`.
findings.issue: `Model.ofPolynomial_H_of_mem_Icc` names only one of the two load-bearing hypotheses; the conclusion also needs `|xi| ≤ 1`, and without it H is 0, so the name suggests Icc membership alone suffices.

findings.evidence: MomentDeterminacy.lean:157-159 conclusion has four conjuncts including `¬ … =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc a b)] 0`; Determinacy.lean:175 `exists_models_forall_le_mellinMomentH_eq_and_H_not_ae_eq` names the analogous clause.
findings.issue: `exists_polynomial_ne_zero_forall_le_setIntegral_Icc_pow_mul_eq_zero` names only `p ≠ 0`, omitting the `¬ (fun x => p.eval x) =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc a b)] 0` clause that the docstring calls the point of the statement; the GPD counterpart does name it (`…_and_H_not_ae_eq`), so the pair is inconsistent and the weaker-sounding name is what a consumer finds.

summary: Names are mostly conclusion-describing and consistent with GPD precedent, but `Model.ofPolynomial` collides with the established GPD meaning of "polynomial" and hides the quark-half restriction, and two names under-describe their statements.
